findings.description: Claim 'a well-documented pattern in software engineering' asserts documentation without citing specific sources. Fair witness discipline requires grounding general knowledge claims.
findings.suggestion: Add a citation — e.g., Parnas (1972) on information hiding, or Brooks (1975) on accidental vs. essential complexity — or soften to 'a widely recognized pattern.'
findings.context: Hard-coding every behavior tends to produce brittle systems (a well-documented pattern in software engineering).

findings.description: 'Invariant 3' references internal project terminology without glossary entry or definition. External readers of the blog lack context for numbered invariants.
findings.suggestion: Either add a glossary entry for 'structural invariants' or expand inline — e.g., 'the coupled generators principle (the third of five structural invariants grounding the governance framework)' — with a link to the governance documentation.

findings.description: Design assertion about premature pruning risk stated as fact without grounding citation. The claim follows logically from the synaptic pruning literature but lacks explicit support.
findings.suggestion: Frame as design judgment rather than fact — e.g., 'We adopted a conservative threshold because premature pruning risks losing rare-firing patterns...' — or cite pruning literature (Huttenlocher, 1979) explicitly in this sentence.
findings.context: Premature pruning risks losing rare-firing patterns that carry high value when they do fire.
